dcterms:title: SMART Trust demonstrator: journeys J1 to J4

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Birth clinic issuing system
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The hospital system abroad that issues a DVC per dose with the HCERT library: the HCERT issuing system (smart-trust-tools) of a trust network participant (XXR).

**Persona**: Software that calls the library once per dose and never holds the private key; signs only with a DSC its country's CSCA issued and has already shared with the GDHCN.

**Also known as**: Issuer of the birth-dose DVCs (SMART Trust Issuer)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- Chiang Rai Provincial Hospital system, Thailand (Country A, XXR)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J1 — Born abroad](scenarios.html#j1--born-abroad-thailand-birth-day): J1 A Lao baby is born in Thailand

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J1 Issue the newborn's birth-dose DVCs in Country A](business-processes.html#j1-issue-the-newborns-birth-dose-dvcs-in-country-a): Build one DVCMinPreQual payload per dose; Prepare: CWT claims and the COSE Sig_structure; Finish: COSE_Sign1, deflate, Base45, HC1:

**Data sets its tasks record or read**: [TD.J1 Birth-dose DVC](dictionary.html#tdj1-birth-dose-dvc)

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Birth clinic vaccinator
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The clinician abroad who gives the birth doses and hands over the signed paper DVC (J1).

**Persona**: A maternity-ward clinician who records doses in the hospital system and prints what it produces.

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- ![Dr. Anan](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) [Dr. Anan](personas.html#dr-anan-thai-clinician--birth--follow-up-thailand), Dr Anan (clinician, Chiang Rai, Thailand)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J1 — Born abroad](scenarios.html#j1--born-abroad-thailand-birth-day): J1 A Lao baby is born in Thailand (told through Dr. Anan)

**User stories** ([all stories](scenarios.html#user-stories)):

- I want to print a signed record of each birth dose the family can carry anywhere

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J1 Issue the newborn's birth-dose DVCs in Country A](business-processes.html#j1-issue-the-newborns-birth-dose-dvcs-in-country-a): Give Hep B and BCG birth doses and record them; Print the paper DVC, one QR per dose

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Caregiver
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The parent who holds the child's paper DVCs and the family phone, and presents them; IHE ITI VHL VHL Holder and smart-trust Holder.

**Persona**: A parent carrying a newborn's records across borders on paper and one shared phone; no health training, little time, limited connectivity.

**Also known as**: VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL); Holder (SMART Trust)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- ![Bounmy](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) [Bounmy](personas.html#bounmy-father--holds-the-family-phone-lao-pdr), Bounmy SENGMANY (father, holds the family phone)
- ![Khamla](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) [Khamla](personas.html#khamla-mother-lao-pdr), Khamla SENGMANY (mother)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J1 — Born abroad](scenarios.html#j1--born-abroad-thailand-birth-day): J1 A Lao baby is born in Thailand
- [J2 — Found at home](scenarios.html#j2--found-at-home-lao-pdr-3-weeks-later): J2a A health worker finds the baby — and reads his cards; J2b Registered at home, and referred
- [J3 — Made official](scenarios.html#j3--made-official-vientiane-district-health-center-4-weeks-later): J3a The clinic confirms the cards are genuine; J3b Thai vaccines are fitted to the Lao schedule
- [J4.0 — Crossing back: one family, one phone](scenarios.html#j40--crossing-back-one-family-one-phone-lao-pdr-12-months-later): J4.0a One phone holds the whole family’s records (told through Bounmy); J4.0b Dad creates a link to share at the clinic (told through Bounmy)
- [J4.1 — Crossing back: a Thai doctor sees the full history](scenarios.html#j41--crossing-back-a-thai-doctor-sees-the-full-history-chiang-rai-12-months-later): J4.1 A Thai doctor sees the full history

**User stories** ([all stories](scenarios.html#user-stories)):

- I want to have my son's birth doses from abroad recognised at home, so that his care does not start over and nothing is repeated
- I want to show each family member's records abroad from our one shared phone, with a passcode I can say aloud, so that a doctor abroad can treat us without paper or an app
- I want to decide who sees my child's record, and for how long, so that the record stays at home and I know who has looked

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J1 Issue the newborn's birth-dose DVCs in Country A](business-processes.html#j1-issue-the-newborns-birth-dose-dvcs-in-country-a): its lane holds no task
- [J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B](business-processes.html#j2-discover-and-refer-an-unregistered-infant-in-country-b): Show the paper DVCs from Country A
- [J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic](business-processes.html#j3-verify-import-and-schedule-at-the-home-clinic): its lane holds no task
- [J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs](business-processes.html#j40-issue-the-familys-records-to-one-phone-as-vhls): Choose who to share, with a passcode and an expiry
- [J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad](business-processes.html#j41-read-a-family-members-records-at-the-point-of-care-abroad): its lane holds no task

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: CHW app
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The OHS app on the CHW's phone: reads a foreign DVC without verifying it (triage read, STT-VER-011), registers the child and records a referral, all offline, syncing later.

**Persona**: Offline-first Android app; must never present an unverified record as verified.

**Also known as**: Triage reader (SMART Trust Receiver, read-unverified)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- CHW app, Lao PDR (Country B)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J2 — Found at home](scenarios.html#j2--found-at-home-lao-pdr-3-weeks-later): J2a A health worker finds the baby — and reads his cards; J2b Registered at home, and referred

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B](business-processes.html#j2-discover-and-refer-an-unregistered-infant-in-country-b): Read each DVC unverified (triage); Add the infant; save doses as reported; Create a referral to the home clinic for verification

**Decisions it makes**:

- Decision table [TD.DT.01 What does a scanned DVC become in the child's record?](decision-logic.html#tddt01-what-does-a-scanned-dvc-become-in-the-childs-record), in: Read each DVC unverified (triage); Add the infant; save doses as reported

**Data sets its tasks record or read**: [TD.J2A Newborn registration on a home visit](dictionary.html#tdj2a-newborn-registration-on-a-home-visit); [TD.J2B Referral for verification](dictionary.html#tdj2b-referral-for-verification)

**Indicators that count its decisions**: [TD.IND.01 Foreign doses imported as verified](indicators.html#tdind01-foreign-doses-imported-as-verified); [TD.IND.03 CHW referrals for verification completed at the clinic](indicators.html#tdind03-chw-referrals-for-verification-completed-at-the-clinic)

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Community health worker
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
Finds unregistered children on home visits, registers them and refers them to the clinic (J2).

**Persona**: Works on foot and offline, on a cheap Android phone; registers and refers, never judges authenticity.

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- ![Vilay](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) [Vilay](personas.html#vilay-community-health-worker--village-04-lao-pdr), Vilay (community health worker, Village 04, Lao PDR)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J2 — Found at home](scenarios.html#j2--found-at-home-lao-pdr-3-weeks-later): J2a A health worker finds the baby — and reads his cards (told through Vilay); J2b Registered at home, and referred (told through Vilay)

**User stories** ([all stories](scenarios.html#user-stories)):

- I want to read a foreign vaccination QR offline and register the child with it, so that the clinic sees what was given before the family arrives
- I want to refer a child whose foreign record needs checking, so that verification is done by someone who can
- I want to register a newborn into the household offline, before civil registration, so that no newborn in my village is missed, even with no signal

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B](business-processes.html#j2-discover-and-refer-an-unregistered-infant-in-country-b): Scan each QR with the CHW app; Explain the referral to the family

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Family phone
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The one smartphone the family shares, holding one VHL QR per member (J4); holds links, not keys to anyone's records beyond what each link grants.

**Persona**: A shared Android phone, sometimes offline; whoever holds it can show any member's QR, the passcode protects the records.

**Also known as**: Personal health wallet

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- The family's shared phone

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J4.0 — Crossing back: one family, one phone](scenarios.html#j40--crossing-back-one-family-one-phone-lao-pdr-12-months-later): J4.0b Dad creates a link to share at the clinic
- [J4.1 — Crossing back: a Thai doctor sees the full history](scenarios.html#j41--crossing-back-a-thai-doctor-sees-the-full-history-chiang-rai-12-months-later): J4.1 A Thai doctor sees the full history

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs](business-processes.html#j40-issue-the-familys-records-to-one-phone-as-vhls): Store each member's VHL QR on the phone
- [J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad](business-processes.html#j41-read-a-family-members-records-at-the-point-of-care-abroad): Show the child's VHL QR

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: GDHCN trust anchor
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
WHO's GDHCN, which receives participants' PKI material and distributes it as DID trust lists; Trust Network Anchor (SMART Trust), Trust Anchor (IHE ITI VHL).

**Persona**: A WHO service publishing DID documents over did:web; verifiers fetch it when online and keep a copy.

**Also known as**: Trust Network Anchor (SMART Trust); Trust Anchor (IHE ITI VHL)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- GDHCN DEV trust network (WHO)

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Home clinic EHR
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The clinic's OHS-based record system: verifies DVCs against the GDHCN trust list, imports them as FHIR Immunization resources and evaluates the national schedule (J3).

**Persona**: Holds the DID trust list from its last refresh, about weekly for a clinic without its own connection, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office; loading it is a precondition of a visit, and it verifies offline at the point of care.

**Also known as**: Verifier at the home clinic (SMART Trust Receiver)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- Vientiane District Health Center EHR (Country B)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J3 — Made official](scenarios.html#j3--made-official-vientiane-district-health-center-4-weeks-later): J3a The clinic confirms the cards are genuine; J3b Thai vaccines are fitted to the Lao schedule

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic](business-processes.html#j3-verify-import-and-schedule-at-the-home-clinic): Verify each HCERT against the trust list; Import the doses as FHIR Immunization resources; Add national codes beside foreign ones; Evaluate the national schedule

**Decisions it makes**:

- Decision table [TD.DT.01 What does a scanned DVC become in the child's record?](decision-logic.html#tddt01-what-does-a-scanned-dvc-become-in-the-childs-record), in: Verify each HCERT against the trust list; Every DVC verified?; Import the doses as FHIR Immunization resources
- Decision table [TD.DT.02 Which national schedule code does an imported dose carry?](decision-logic.html#tddt02-which-national-schedule-code-does-an-imported-dose-carry), in: Add national codes beside foreign ones
- Decision table [TD.DT.03 Does the national schedule count this dose?](decision-logic.html#tddt03-does-the-national-schedule-count-this-dose), in: Evaluate the national schedule
- Decision table [TD.DT.04 Is this dose of the national schedule due?](decision-logic.html#tddt04-is-this-dose-of-the-national-schedule-due), in: Evaluate the national schedule
- Gateway "Every DVC verified?" in [J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic](business-processes.html#j3-verify-import-and-schedule-at-the-home-clinic)

**Data sets its tasks record or read**: [TD.J3A DVC verification and import](dictionary.html#tdj3a-dvc-verification-and-import); [TD.J3B Imported dose and schedule](dictionary.html#tdj3b-imported-dose-and-schedule)

**Indicators that count its decisions**: [TD.IND.01 Foreign doses imported as verified](indicators.html#tdind01-foreign-doses-imported-as-verified); [TD.IND.03 CHW referrals for verification completed at the clinic](indicators.html#tdind03-chw-referrals-for-verification-completed-at-the-clinic); [TD.IND.04 Imported doses carrying a national schedule code](indicators.html#tdind04-imported-doses-carrying-a-national-schedule-code)

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Home clinic provider
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The nurse at the home clinic who receives the referral, has the foreign DVCs verified and decides catch-up doses (J3).

**Persona**: Trusts the system's verdict and needs a reason when a certificate fails.

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- ![Chanthasone](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) [Chanthasone](personas.html#chanthasone-nurse--district-health-center-lao-pdr), Nurse Chanthasone (Vientiane District Health Center, Lao PDR)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J3 — Made official](scenarios.html#j3--made-official-vientiane-district-health-center-4-weeks-later): J3a The clinic confirms the cards are genuine (told through Chanthasone); J3b Thai vaccines are fitted to the Lao schedule (told through Chanthasone)

**User stories** ([all stories](scenarios.html#user-stories)):

- I want to know whether a foreign certificate is genuine, and why not when it is not
- I want to see which doses are due once the foreign doses are imported, so that I give only what is missing
- I want to keep the foreign vaccine code and add our schedule code beside it, deciding myself when there is no match, so that the other country's record is never overwritten and the next nurse need not decide again

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic](business-processes.html#j3-verify-import-and-schedule-at-the-home-clinic): Scan the QRs and open the referral; Note the failure; decide doses by policy; Give due doses and book the next visit

**Decisions it makes**:

- Decision table [TD.DT.01 What does a scanned DVC become in the child's record?](decision-logic.html#tddt01-what-does-a-scanned-dvc-become-in-the-childs-record), in: Note the failure; decide doses by policy
- Decision table [TD.DT.04 Is this dose of the national schedule due?](decision-logic.html#tddt04-is-this-dose-of-the-national-schedule-due), in: Give due doses and book the next visit

**Data sets its tasks record or read**: [TD.J2B Referral for verification](dictionary.html#tdj2b-referral-for-verification); [TD.J3A DVC verification and import](dictionary.html#tdj3a-dvc-verification-and-import); [TD.J3B Imported dose and schedule](dictionary.html#tdj3b-imported-dose-and-schedule)

**Indicators that count its decisions**: [TD.IND.01 Foreign doses imported as verified](indicators.html#tdind01-foreign-doses-imported-as-verified); [TD.IND.03 CHW referrals for verification completed at the clinic](indicators.html#tdind03-chw-referrals-for-verification-completed-at-the-clinic)

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Issuer signing key
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The DSC private key of the issuing participant, in an HSM, cloud KMS or Android Keystore; signs the bytes the issuing system prepares (two-phase signing, STT-ISS-004).

**Persona**: A key that signs what it is given and reveals nothing else.

**Also known as**: Document signer (DSC) key

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- XXR document signer key (Country A, Thailand)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J1 — Born abroad](scenarios.html#j1--born-abroad-thailand-birth-day): J1 A Lao baby is born in Thailand
- [J4.0 — Crossing back: one family, one phone](scenarios.html#j40--crossing-back-one-family-one-phone-lao-pdr-12-months-later): J4.0b Dad creates a link to share at the clinic

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J1 Issue the newborn's birth-dose DVCs in Country A](business-processes.html#j1-issue-the-newborns-birth-dose-dvcs-in-country-a): Sign the bytes with XXR's DSC key
- [J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs](business-processes.html#j40-issue-the-familys-records-to-one-phone-as-vhls): Sign with Country B's DSC key

**Data sets its tasks record or read**: [TD.J1 Birth-dose DVC](dictionary.html#tdj1-birth-dose-dvc)

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: National health portal
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The home country's portal that issues each family member's records (IPS, DVCs) as a passcode-protected Verifiable Health Link and hosts the manifests (J4.0), checking the passcode, expiry and consent on each request and logging every access at home (J4.1): the VHL Sharer.

**Persona**: A government service signing with the national DSC, issued under the national CSCA and already shared with the GDHCN; hosts manifests and encrypted documents for a limited time.

**Also known as**: VHL Sharer (IHE ITI VHL); Issuer of the family's VHLs (SMART Trust Issuer)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- Lao PDR national health portal and gateway (Country B, XXH)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J4.0 — Crossing back: one family, one phone](scenarios.html#j40--crossing-back-one-family-one-phone-lao-pdr-12-months-later): J4.0b Dad creates a link to share at the clinic
- [J4.1 — Crossing back: a Thai doctor sees the full history](scenarios.html#j41--crossing-back-a-thai-doctor-sees-the-full-history-chiang-rai-12-months-later): J4.1 A Thai doctor sees the full history

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs](business-processes.html#j40-issue-the-familys-records-to-one-phone-as-vhls): Assemble each member's IPS and DVCs; Encrypt, publish a passcode manifest; Prepare the HCERT carrying the VHL at key 5; Finish the HC1 QR text
- [J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad](business-processes.html#j41-read-a-family-members-records-at-the-point-of-care-abroad): Check passcode, log access, return manifest

**Decisions it makes**:

- Decision table [TD.DT.05 Does the portal release the manifest for this request?](decision-logic.html#tddt05-does-the-portal-release-the-manifest-for-this-request), in: Check passcode, log access, return manifest

**Data sets its tasks record or read**: [TD.J40 Shared link and consent](dictionary.html#tdj40-shared-link-and-consent); [TD.J41 Access to a shared link](dictionary.html#tdj41-access-to-a-shared-link)

**Indicators that count its decisions**: [TD.IND.02 Shared-link openings that were authorised](indicators.html#tdind02-shared-link-openings-that-were-authorised)

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Point-of-care provider
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The clinician abroad who scans the family's QR and reads the child's records (J4.1).

**Persona**: Has minutes, no prior relationship with the family, and her own hospital's system.

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- ![Dr. Anan](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) [Dr. Anan](personas.html#dr-anan-thai-clinician--birth--follow-up-thailand), Dr Anan (clinician, Chiang Rai, Thailand)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J4.1 — Crossing back: a Thai doctor sees the full history](scenarios.html#j41--crossing-back-a-thai-doctor-sees-the-full-history-chiang-rai-12-months-later): J4.1 A Thai doctor sees the full history (told through Dr. Anan)

**User stories** ([all stories](scenarios.html#user-stories)):

- I want to read a visiting child's summary and vaccinations from a QR the parent shows, so that without installing anything or calling another country
- I want to know the record I read abroad came from the child's home country and was not altered, so that I can rely on it as I would on my own clinic's record

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad](business-processes.html#j41-read-a-family-members-records-at-the-point-of-care-abroad): Scan the QR and enter the passcode the caregiver says; Not verified: treat records as paper; Review history, allergies and vaccinations

**Decisions it makes**:

- Decision table [TD.DT.06 Does the receiver follow the VHL?](decision-logic.html#tddt06-does-the-receiver-follow-the-vhl), in: Not verified: treat records as paper

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Point-of-care receiver
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The clinic system abroad that scans a VHL, verifies it, fetches the manifest (ITI-YY5) and decrypts the documents (J4.1): the VHL Receiver.

**Persona**: A hospital system on a trust network with its own receiver key; its DID trust list is a cache refreshed nightly or hourly, loaded before a visit, so it verifies without being online.

**Also known as**: VHL Receiver (IHE ITI VHL); Receiver of the family's VHLs (SMART Trust Receiver)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- Chiang Rai primary care clinic viewer, Thailand (J4.1)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J4.1 — Crossing back: a Thai doctor sees the full history](scenarios.html#j41--crossing-back-a-thai-doctor-sees-the-full-history-chiang-rai-12-months-later): J4.1 A Thai doctor sees the full history

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad](business-processes.html#j41-read-a-family-members-records-at-the-point-of-care-abroad): Verify the HCERT and read the VHL at key 5; Request the manifest (ITI-YY5), signed; Decrypt the IPS and DVCs

**Decisions it makes**:

- Decision table [TD.DT.06 Does the receiver follow the VHL?](decision-logic.html#tddt06-does-the-receiver-follow-the-vhl), in: Verify the HCERT and read the VHL at key 5; HCERT verified?; Request the manifest (ITI-YY5), signed
- Gateway "HCERT verified?" in [J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad](business-processes.html#j41-read-a-family-members-records-at-the-point-of-care-abroad)

**Data sets its tasks record or read**: [TD.J41 Access to a shared link](dictionary.html#tdj41-access-to-a-shared-link)

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Subject of care
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
The person the records are about: the child whose doses are given, signed, registered, verified and shared. Acts through the caregiver, holds no device and plays no lane in the journeys' processes.

**Persona**: A newborn whose vaccination history must follow him across a border he cannot speak for.

**Also known as**: Patient; Care recipient

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- ![Somsack](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) [Somsack](personas.html#somsack-baby--the-record-follows-him-lao-pdr), Somsack SENGMANY (newborn)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J1 — Born abroad](scenarios.html#j1--born-abroad-thailand-birth-day): J1 A Lao baby is born in Thailand
- [J2 — Found at home](scenarios.html#j2--found-at-home-lao-pdr-3-weeks-later): J2b Registered at home, and referred
- [J4.1 — Crossing back: a Thai doctor sees the full history](scenarios.html#j41--crossing-back-a-thai-doctor-sees-the-full-history-chiang-rai-12-months-later): J4.1 A Thai doctor sees the full history

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: TD.DT.01 What does a scanned DVC become in the child's record?
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description: From the result of reading one foreign DVC, decide whether its dose is recorded as verified, kept as reported and not verified, or not recorded from it at all. schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: TD.DT.02 Which national schedule code does an imported dose carry?

schema:hasPart.dcterms:description: The national map the clinic EHR uses in J3 to add the schedule code beside the issuer's product code, which it never replaces. The Hep B product had no entry until Nurse Chanthasone confirmed its equivalence on 2025-11-25 (see TrustDemoJ3Adjudication); her decision is recorded here so the next clinic need not make it again.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: TD.J1 Birth-dose DVC
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description: What the birth hospital records for each birth dose and signs into one Digital Vaccination Certificate (DVC, an HCERT) per dose: the payload, the CWT claims and the key that signs it.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: TD.J2B Referral for verification
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description: The community health worker's referral of the child to the home clinic, to verify the foreign cards and fit the doses to the national schedule.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: TD.J2A Newborn registration on a home visit
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description: What the community health worker records offline when she finds a newborn missing from the household roster: the registration form's answers and each dose read from a foreign card without verifying it.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: TD.J3A DVC verification and import
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description: What the clinic records when it verifies a foreign DVC against its cached copy of the trust list, and, when the DVC verifies, imports the dose in place of the reported one.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: TD.J3B Imported dose and schedule
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description: What the clinic records for each imported dose's vaccine code, and what the national schedule finds due once the doses are counted.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: TD.J41 Access to a shared link
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description: What the home country logs for every request to open a shared link, released or refused.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: TD.J40 Shared link and consent
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description: What the home country records when the holder shares a family member's summary as a Verifiable Health Link (VHL): who may read what, for how long, and that a passcode protects it.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Lao PDR: foreign DVC verified against the GDHCN trust list
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
How it is used: J3a. The district EHR verifies each Thai DVC offline against its cached copy of the GDHCN trust list, then imports the dose. This record says so.

Why: a verified dose replaces a reported one, so the record must show who verified what, against which policy, and which reported doses it removes. Anyone who later doubts a dose can follow this record back to the signed certificate and the issuing country's key.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Lao PDR: household on the CHW's roster
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
How it is used: J2a. The CHW finds that a newborn is missing from the household roster and adds Somsack as a member.

Why: Lao community health work is organized by household. The roster is how a CHW notices that a child is missing, and it is the unit the family phone shares under in J4 (one phone, three profiles).

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Lao PDR: dose on the national schedule
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
How it is used: J3 and after. These are the Thai birth doses once the district clinic has verified them, and every dose given in Lao PDR.

Why: the Lao schedule engine works on Lao EPI codes, so each dose must carry one. A dose that came from abroad keeps the issuer's product code beside the Lao one, added through the ConceptMap and confirmed by the nurse. Nothing the other country said is overwritten. A verified foreign dose is recorded from its primary source, the signing hospital, and its Provenance says how it was verified.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Lao PDR: child registered by the community health worker
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
How it is used: J2 onwards. Vilay registers Somsack on a home visit, and the same patient carries every Lao record that follows: the verified Thai doses, the Lao doses and the summary shared in J4.

Why: a child born abroad is not in the Lao civil registry yet. A temporary id lets the CHW, the district clinic and the national portal all refer to the same child until civil registration catches up. The parents are recorded as contacts, because they hold the paper cards and later the family's VHLs.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Lao PDR: CHW referral to verify foreign cards
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
How it is used: J2b. The CHW refers Somsack to the district health center to have his foreign cards verified and his doses fitted to the Lao schedule.

Why: the CHW cannot verify a DVC on the phone, but the clinic can. The referral points at the reported doses it is about, so the clinic knows exactly what to check, and the CHW can see when it is done.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Lao PDR: newborn registration captured offline
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
How it is used: J2a. These are the CHW's answers on the newborn registration form, which the app renders with Structured Data Capture and saves with no signal.

Why: in Lao PDR the form is the configuration, not code. A ministry can change the questions without shipping a new app. The answers are kept so that the Patient and Group extracted from them can always be traced back to what was asked and who answered.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Lao PDR: foreign dose as reported (not yet verified)
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
How it is used: J2b. The CHW app reads each Thai paper DVC offline without checking its signature, and saves the dose like this.

Why: a CHW phone may have no trust list and no signal, but the doses should not be lost. Recording them with primarySource false and the family as the information source keeps them visibly "reported, not verified". The schedule will not count them until a clinic verifies them (J3). Only the issuer's product code is present, because mapping to the Lao schedule is a clinical step for later.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Lao PDR: every VHL access logged at home
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
How it is used: J4.1. The Lao national gateway records each attempt by a clinic abroad to fetch a family member's VHL manifest, the refused ones included.

Why: the family shares a link, not a copy, and the data stays in Lao PDR. Logging every access at home, following IHE Basic Audit Log Patterns, is what lets the family and the ministry see who looked, from where and when. A wrong passcode is logged too.

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Thailand: dose given at the birth hospital (DVC source)
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
How it is used: J1. Each birth dose (Hep B, BCG) that Dr Anan gives is recorded here first. The hospital then packs it into a Digital Vaccination Certificate (HCERT, signed with XXR's key) and prints it as a QR card.

Why: the DVC can only carry what this record holds. The vaccine product, date, lot, dose number and the administering organization are exactly the fields the HCERT certificate needs. They are required here so every printed card is complete. The product is coded from the WHO PreQual-style product list, because that is the code Lao PDR will later map to its own schedule (J3).

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Thailand: newborn at the birth hospital
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
How it is used: J1. Chiang Rai Provincial Hospital registers Somsack under its own hospital number on the day he is born.

Why: a baby born to Lao parents in Thailand has no Thai citizen id, so the hospital number is the only identifier the hospital can put behind the dose records it signs. The DVCs it prints carry the name and date of birth, not this number. The family's home country therefore cannot rely on any Thai identifier, and links the doses to its own patient (see the Lao patient profile).

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: Thailand: record of a summary read through a VHL
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description:
How it is used: J4.1. The Chiang Rai clinic viewer keeps this record when it opens Somsack's patient summary through the Verifiable Health Link that his father shows.

Why: the Thai clinic views the Lao record and does not copy it into a Thai registry. So the clinic keeps a note of what it saw, where it came from, and how it was verified: the VHL's signature against Lao PDR's key on the GDHCN trust list, the manifest fetch, and the passcode. The Lao side keeps its own log of the same access (the Lao audit profile).

schema:hasPart.dcterms:title: SMART Trust demonstrator: journeys J1 to J4
schema:hasPart.dcterms:description: The user journeys of one cross-border family, as the VaxLink walkthrough tells them (birth-dose DVCs in Thailand, CHW registration and triage read in Lao PDR, clinic verification, vaccine-code mapping and schedule, family VHLs on one phone, viewed and audited back in Thailand) as a WHO SMART Guidelines L2 DAK and L3 implementation guide, built on the SMART Trust HCERT libraries.
